text:
ava: heads-up: found a reproducible token drift when we insert a tiny system prompt mid-generation on q3-int3hybrid
diego: which build and sequence len?
ava: magnet-13b-q3-int3hyb, seq=32k, reinject at ~12k tokens. fp32 baseline clean, q3 shows token skip/insert ~12,042.
sophia: any flags toggled? rotary_rescale / pack_stride?
ava: rotary_rescale helps but doesn't fully fix. pack_stride appears to matter.
diego: paste the minimal repro and short logs?
ava: repro (simplified):
```
POST /v1/generate
{"model":"magnet-13b-q3","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"S1\n"},{"role":"user","content":"<LONG_USER>"}]}
# programmatically insert {"role":"system","content":"S2\n"} mid-run
```
logs snippet:
[2026-04-02T08:12:11Z] kv_pack_offset: 1324
[2026-04-02T08:12:11Z] rope_anchor_base: 0x2c88 -> 0x2c78 (delta -16)
[2026-04-02T08:12:11Z] next_token(actual): "ing" vs expected "ed"
sophia: delta -16 consistent with pointer rounding in packed KV write. hypothesis: small-insert writes change block-relative offsets, shifting RoPE base mapping for some attention heads.
diego: quick experiments: (1) pad S2 to pack_stride boundary; (2) prefix_cache_disable=true; (3) run quant4-hybrid.
ava: ran (1) and (2): both eliminate the drift in my env. (3) queued.
sophia: good signal. plan: add lightweight instrumentation to canary: kv_pack_offset, rope_anchor_base, head_phase_checksum, top5_logits around injection; run 30 trials fp32/q3/q3+rescale/q4hyb on dedicated GPU.
diego: if confirmed, fix options: allocate tiny-insert writes with stable-offset policy OR do a fast re-anchor after any midstream prompt reinsertion. also add regression in longcontext-suite.
deploy-bot: canary image magnet-13b-q3-anchorpatch deployed to pool-canary-4 (sha: b6f2a1)
ava: filing issue ML-12201 with attached diffs and logs, will upload harness results EOD.
sophia: thanks, this is a clear path. tag eng-runtime and eng-sre for allocator parity checks. :mag:
_meta: generated slack thread about KV packing + RoPE anchor drift during mid-generation system prompt insertion; concise slack-style messages and short logs
